title: Proper time formatting for locales where AMPM is going in front of time value
line: In locales like Korean the clock now shows AM/PM before the time, as the locale does.
explanation: The digital clock's timeFormatCorrection() threw away the locale's short time format and rebuilt it as hours, separator, minutes and then " AP", so the AM/PM marker always came after the time. Korean (and other locales such as Chinese) put it first, so the panel showed '11:29 오전' instead of '오전 11:29'. The change adds a small TimeFormat helper in the applet's plugin that edits the locale's format in place: it only switches the hour cycle (adding " AP" after the time when 12-hour is forced on a 24-hour locale, removing the marker when 24-hour is forced) and adds or removes the seconds.

commits.message:
applets/digital-clock: Keep AM/PM where the locale puts it

The clock rebuilt its time format as hours, minutes and " AP", so AM/PM
always came after the time, even in Korean where it comes first. Edit
the locale's own format instead, changing only its hours and seconds.

BUG: 408662

media.caption: Master, LC_TIME=ko_KR: panel '11:29 오전', tooltip '11:29:01 오전' (marker after the time)
With the fix, LC_TIME=ko_KR: panel '오후 4:55', tooltip '오후 4:55:13' (marker first, as Korean does)

review.text: Fixes the cause: timeFormatCorrection() threw away the locale's format and always appended ' AP' after the time. The new C++ TimeFormat helper edits the locale's short format in place, only switching the hour cycle and seconds, so Korean/Chinese keep the marker first and separators and padding are kept. The forced-24h zero padding from master and the en_US/de_DE/ko_KR cases were all checked. It is more code than a regex tweak, but it's cleaner and testable (it would be worth adding a small autotest for withHourCycle/withSeconds). It overlaps plasma-workspace!6498, so that MR should be coordinated with this one.
